Traditional Colcannon

Served at: Imbolc Day Celebration · Saint Patrick's Day

Serves 4-6Prep 20 minCook 30 min

Colcannon is a beloved Irish dish, a comforting and hearty mash of potatoes and cabbage or kale, often enjoyed during colder months. It holds special significance for Imbolc, a Celtic festival marking the beginning of spring, symbolizing the return of green vegetables, and is a cherished staple for Saint Patrick's Day celebrations, offering a taste of Irish heritage.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900g) Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and quartered
  • 1/2 head (about 1 pound / 450g) green cabbage, cored and shredded, or 1 bunch (about 8 ounces / 225g) kale, stems removed and chopped
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) whole milk or heavy cream
  • 1/4 cup (55g) unsalted butter, plus extra for serving
  • 1 small onion or 4-5 green onions (scallions), thinly sliced (white and light green parts)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

Method

  1. Place the peeled and quartered potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
  2. While the potatoes are cooking, melt 2 tablespoons (28g) of butter in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the shredded cabbage or chopped kale and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 5-10 minutes. If using onion, add it with the cabbage and cook until softened.
  3. Drain the cooked potatoes thoroughly and return them to the empty pot. Mash the potatoes until smooth.
  4. In a small saucepan, gently heat the milk or cream with the remaining 2 tablespoons (28g) of butter until warm. Do not boil.
  5. Pour the warm milk mixture into the mashed potatoes and mix well until creamy.
  6. Fold in the cooked cabbage (and onion/scallions, if using) into the mashed potatoes.
  7. Season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
  8. Serve hot, with an extra pat of butter melting in the center of each serving, if desired.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, use heavy cream instead of whole milk.
  • A pinch of freshly grated nutmeg can be added to the mashed potatoes for an extra layer of warmth.
  • Leftover colcannon can be pan-fried the next day for a delicious crispy texture.
